summary: Oversize drop is silent to producers: emit returns the event but never fans out; callers cannot distinguish delivered vs dropped (no flag/counter). Persistence comment claims oversized never reach here but no metric counts drops.

MAX_LISTENERS=100 on a single shared EventEmitter: ~2 permanent onAny + 1 message:new + 1 per approval-wait + tests; burst approvals or repeated registerSocketServer in tests can approach ceiling; warn threshold 500 counts map entries not emitter listeners so the two guards disagree.

Two broker handles (globalBroker + sharedBroker) with 3-way fallback chain; worker-local broker documented local-only so worker emits (approval sweeper expiry, maintenance snapshot) never reach API sockets or the JSONL log.

approval.requested emit is best-effort warn-and-skip when no broker is registered; the run is already WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL (transition before emit) so a dropped event strands the fast path on the DB poll fallback with no alert.
Fan-out is fully synchronous: one slow onAny/on subscriber (JSONL append dispatch excluded - detached; but socket emit + IndexBuilder await) blocks all later subscribers in the same emit call.

event-types.ts depends (types-only) on messages/message-gate.js, runs/runs-gate.js for ChannelMessage/RunStatus; a future value import would create a gate-to-gate cycle risk. Today type-only, no violation.
Scope creep: Mode/isValidMode (composer mode validation) rides the broker gate; unrelated contract bundled with pub/sub surface.
